title: trajectory-judge: measuring what LLM judges miss when an agent reaches the right answer the wrong way
description: A controlled comparison of how well LLM judges detect faults in tool-using agent trajectories, under conditions where the ground truth is known by construction. A synthetic support-desk environment with a scripted oracle policy provides known-correct behaviour; a six-type fault injector then breaks exactly one step at a known index and records whether the customer-visible outcome survived, which stratifies failures into silent and loud. Five judges - a programmatic rule checker, an outcome-only judge, a step-rubric judge at two model sizes, and a self-consistency ensemble - are scored on detection, step localisation, failure-type classification, calibration and cost over 400 trajectories. Every raw verdict is committed, so all tables and figures rebuild offline with no model calls.
